title: Medical tests start for Malaysia-bound workers at 51 approved centres
excerpt: Screening announced for 31 October has begun. Workers pay Tk 8,000 at Malaysia-approved centres, and unapproved centres face closure.
content:
Full medical screening for workers going to Malaysia has started at centres approved under Malaysia's Foreign Workers Centralised Management System (FWCMS), the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare said, bdnews24.com reported on 16 November.

The tests had been due to start on 31 October but did not. A ministry official said the reason for the delay was unclear. There are 51 approved centres and the test costs Tk 8,000. Unapproved centres and recruiting agencies are barred from carrying out tests, and those that break the rule face closure or suspension of their overseas recruitment.

A government-managed drive to send 10,000 workers at zero migration cost is under way, with 112 men in the final selection for DHL Supply Chain (Malaysia). Malaysia is also set to list 338 Bangladeshi recruiting agencies. Ariful Haque Choudhury is the Expatriates' Welfare Minister.

Why it matters

Who carries out medical tests, and at what price, decides part of what workers pay to migrate. Tighter control could protect workers, but a Tk 8,000 fee sits uneasily with promises of zero-cost migration. The move follows the government's cap of Tk 1.54 lakh on the cost of going to Malaysia, and migrant-rights NGOs will want to check what workers actually pay.

What to watch

Whether workers are charged more than the set fee, how the 338 agencies are chosen, and how many of the 10,000 workers actually leave on zero-cost terms.
